spec_match.rationale: Reads the spec names speechStartTime/speechEndTime first (double seconds on the session audio timeline; web-speech-api index.bs and Chromium main speech_recognition_result.idl, renamed in branch 8078 = M156) and falls back to the Chrome 153-155 draft audioStartTime/audioEndTime (DOMHighResTimeStamp?, verified in tag 153.0.8010.12), labelled as draft. Latency = event.timeStamp - (audiostart event.timeStamp + speechEndTime*1000), with the page and code sample saying the session audio timeline counts consumed audio, so this is an estimate for live mic input.

interactive.rationale: Threshold slider, Start and the labelled sample walkthrough update the verdict and table.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles unsupported recognition; does not explain that the timestamps are on the session audio timeline rather than a wall clock, which affects latency maths.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus.com/feature/<id> in the see-also block plus the spec/explainer.

conformance.rationale: Suite is 8/8 BLOCKED (manual) and every assertion names audioStartTime/audioEndTime, but the spec PR #192 and Chromium's speech_recognition_result.idl define speechStartTime/speechEndTime — the suite cannot pass on a correct implementation. Immutable: needs a human decision, not an agent edit.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Stub-driven test (test-only SpeechRecognition stub, not shipped) exercised the spec, draft and absent result shapes and all three render correctly; a real recognition result cannot be produced headless (no mic/backend), so the live success path is not runtime-verified. Flag banner verified against runtime_enabled_features.json5: WebSpeechTimestamps experimental in branches 8010-8154, stable on Win/Mac/Linux in main.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry is loaded and the page records named assertions for its main measurement; no unexpected errors seen.

design_system.rationale: Inline styles use the design-system variables; button overrides keep text/background pairs readable; not a static card.

accessibility.rationale: Native, labelled controls (no unnamed controls found), visible focus on a Tab walk, and results surfaced as text in status/output regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At 360×740 documentElement.scrollWidth === innerWidth (wide content scrolls inside its own container) and desktop 1280×800 lays out cleanly.

openQuestions.title: Human: the immutable conformance.json describes the wrong names, units and nullability
openQuestions.detail: Every assertion in speechrecognitionresult-timestamps-webspeech-api/conformance.json names audioStartTime/audioEndTime as DOMHighResTimeStamp? milliseconds on the time origin and defines latency as event.timeStamp - audioEndTime. That is the Chrome 153-155 draft. The spec (index.bs) and Chrome 156+ use speechStartTime/speechEndTime, non-nullable double SECONDS on the session audio timeline, so latency needs an audiostart anchor. All assertions are kind manual, so nothing fails, but they no longer describe the contract. The suite is immutable to agents; a human should decide whether to add a new spec-name suite.

guidanceConsulted.query: speech recognition captions transcript live region accessibility
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose transcript/caption updates as text in a polite live region; keep start/stop as native buttons with clear state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Observed: captions/verdicts render as text lists with role=status; start/stop are native buttons.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest search "speech recognition captions transcript live region accessibility" (run 2026-11-15)

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use small non-blocking inline messages, never modals or interstitials, for information that is not a consequential action.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Flag instructions are a static inline role=note callout under the header; no modal or dismiss step; CSS variables only (stone/charcoal, AA); code spans use overflow-wrap:anywhere so the long flag names do not overflow at 360px.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest search "experimental feature flag banner" + retrieve content-first-noise-reduction (run 2026-11-15)

guidanceConsulted.query: removable chip button tap target size
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Make every control at least 24x24 CSS px and 44x44 on touch screens (WCAG 2.5.5); for checkboxes, wrap the input in its label and size the label.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: controls touched by this pass get min-block-size/min-inline-size 44px; measured at 360px.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest search "removable chip button tap target size" + retrieve form-factor-adaptation (run 2026-11-15)
